name: Buying & Storing Meat
summary: Reading labels and dates, how long meat keeps in the fridge and freezer, and freezing it well.

items: Pick up meat last and get it into the fridge within 2 hours (1 hour on a hot day). Bag it separately so juices can't drip onto other food.
Look for firm meat with good color and little liquid in the package. Beef that's brownish inside the pack is usually fine (it's just not exposed to air); a sour smell or slimy feel is not.
**Sell-by** dates are for the store. **Use-by** dates are the maker's advice for best quality. Neither is a safety deadline, but follow the fridge times below from the day you buy it.

sections.heading: How long it keeps
blocks: Times are for a fridge at 40°F (4°C) or colder and a freezer at 0°F (-18°C). Frozen meat stays safe indefinitely; the freezer times are for best quality.

rows: Chicken and turkey, whole or parts
Fish (fatty fish keep less time frozen)

items: Freeze meat as soon as you know you won't cook it in time, not on its last day.
Wrap tightly and squeeze out the air (freezer bags or plastic wrap plus foil) to avoid freezer burn: dry, grayish patches that are safe but taste flat.
Freeze in meal-sized portions and flat, so it freezes and thaws faster.
Label with what it is and the date.
Meat thawed in the fridge can go back in the freezer uncooked; meat thawed in cold water or the microwave should be cooked first. See [thawing safely](guide:doneness-and-food-safety#thawing).
